## Labs

Labs are **not graded**. They are the hands-on companion to each lecture unit. Each lab is a short session: load data, build representations, visualize them, and see what each form makes easy or hides.

::: {.callout-important}
## Midterm and Final

Labs are not graded, but they show what the exams will test.

- **Each unit:** the concepts in that week's code and **Think** questions.
- **Midterm and final:** lecture definitions and formulas, plus the labs covered up to that exam. You will explain *why* a method or representation is used. Library function names and notebook boilerplate will not be tested.
:::

## Datasets

Original files live in the repository `data/` folder, not beside each notebook. Labs import `data.loader`, which finds those files and downloads anything that is missing. Details: `data/README.md`.

You do not copy files into the lab folder. If a file is already under `data/`, it is not downloaded again. Only missing files are fetched.

```bash
pixi run python -m data
```

```python
from data.loader import check_datasets
check_datasets()                # download if missing, then load
check_datasets(download=False)  # local files only
```

| Type | Dataset | Path | Auto-download |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Record | Titanic | `data/record/titanic.csv` | seaborn `sns.load_dataset("titanic")` if missing |
| Record | Iris | `data/record/iris.csv` | `sklearn.datasets.load_iris` if missing |
| Text | 20 Newsgroups | `data/text/20newsgroups/` | `sklearn.datasets.fetch_20newsgroups` if missing |
| Graph | Zachary's Karate Club | `data/graph/karate/` (`nodes.csv`, `edges.csv`) | NetworkX `karate_club_graph()` if missing |
| Graph | Cora | `data/graph/cora/` (`nodes.csv`, `edges.csv`) | [temprl.com/nodes.csv](https://temprl.com/nodes.csv), [temprl.com/edges.csv](https://temprl.com/edges.csv) if missing ([Cora](https://graphsandnetworks.com/the-cora-dataset/)) |
| Interaction | MovieLens 100K | `data/interaction/Movielens/` (`u.data`, `u.item`, `u.user`) | kagglehub [`trishna8/movielens-100k-dataset`](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/trishna8/movielens-100k-dataset) if missing |
| Transaction | Groceries (arules) | `data/transaction/groceries.csv` | shipped in the repo; else GitHub [`stedy/Machine-Learning-with-R-datasets`](https://github.com/stedy/Machine-Learning-with-R-datasets/blob/master/groceries.csv) |
| Transaction | Groceries Kaggle (raw) | `data/transaction/groceries_kaggle(raw).csv` | kagglehub [`heeraldedhia/groceries-dataset`](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/heeraldedhia/groceries-dataset) if missing |
| Transaction | Groceries Kaggle (baskets) | `data/transaction/groceries_kaggle.csv` | built from raw by `(Member_number, Date)` |

Moons (Lab 2-3) is not under `data/`. It comes from `sklearn.datasets.make_moons`.

Do not download files one by one in the browser. If kagglehub asks for auth, get an API token from [Kaggle Settings](https://www.kaggle.com/settings) and put it at `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`.

MovieLens 100K needs a separate GroupLens redistribution permission. The repo ships code only. Each person downloads the data locally.

| Function | Role |
|:---|:---|
| `load_titanic()` | Titanic table |
| `load_iris()` | Iris table |
| `load_20newsgroups()` | 20 Newsgroups documents |
| `ensure_karate()` / `load_karate()` | Karate Club nodes, edges, and graph |
| `ensure_cora()` / `load_cora()` | Cora citation network |
| `ensure_movielens()` / `load_movielens_100k()` / `load_movies()` / `load_users()` | MovieLens folder and tables |
| `ensure_groceries()` / `load_groceries(path)` | arules basket CSV |
| `ensure_groceries_kaggle_raw()` | Kaggle long-format CSV |
| `ensure_groceries_kaggle()` | Kaggle basket CSV |
| `check_datasets()` | load all of the above and return a status table |

## Workflow

### Step 1: Set Up the Environment

Follow [Environment Setup (한)](environment-setup-ko.html) or [Environment Setup (en)](environment-setup-en.html) before opening any lab. Activate the course `pixi` environment so NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, NetworkX, and the other shared packages are available.

### Step 2: Open the Lab Notebook

Launch the notebook with JupyterLab or VS Code from the **repository root**. Open Lab 1 notebooks from `exercises/lab01/` and Lab 2 notebooks from `exercises/lab02/` so helpers import cleanly. `lab01_setup.py` and Lab 2 `helper.py` put the repository root on `sys.path` so `from data.loader import ...` works.

::: {.callout-note}
## Running Cells in Order

Run notebook cells from top to bottom. If you skip a cell or run them out of order, later cells may fail because variables or imports are missing.
:::

### Step 3: Run and Observe

**Lab 0 and Lab 1** do not ask you to fill in `TODO` blocks. Working code is provided. Run the cells, read the notes, and see how the same observations look as a matrix, a graph, a sequence, or a set of transactions. Watch shapes, sparsity, and what was stored versus derived.

**Lab 2:** implement the `TODO` functions in `lab02_*.py` first, restart the kernel, then run the matching notebook from the top. On the course site, Practice outputs are the expected results after those functions are implemented.

### Step 4: Experiment Freely

Labs are for exploration. After you have run the provided code, change things:

- Subsample users, items, documents, or transactions and watch the representations change.
- Swap one representation for another (for example a count matrix vs. TF-IDF, or an adjacency list vs. an adjacency matrix).
- Break things on purpose (a missing path, a wrong key, a dense matrix that should have stayed sparse) and read the error.
